title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LA0RE_0LD---_1RE0LF_1RF0RD_1LD0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LA0RE_0LD---_1RE0LF_1RF0RD_1LD0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Left of the start the tape is a list of blocks of a = 10 separated by s = 01100, with one junction cell j somewhere. Lean proves three kinds of rounds, each for all block lengths: the junction in the first block moves a word over (two more on the left, one fewer on the right); the junction in a later block makes the first block pay one word, the block before the junction gain three and the block after it lose one, the blocks in between being crossed unchanged (proved with up to two blocks between); and with no junction, the first block pays one word into a run of 1001100 words at the right end. The second kind is the tripling: a block of c words that the junction passes comes back as 3c plus a few. Jumping over these rounds, the run is followed exactly (checked against the machine to 1011 steps) to 1012 steps without a halt. What remains is the bounded work where the junction meets a separator or the right end.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 72,856 cells have been visited and 36,256 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Rounds at the left end, for all sizes
claims.text: 0^inf D> 0 (10)^x 0 (10)^(y+1) R reaches 0^inf D> 0 (10)^(x+2) 1 (10)^y R in 4x+10 steps and 0^inf D> 0 (10)^x 1 (10)^(y+1) R reaches 0^inf D> 0 (10)^(x+2) 0 (10)^y R in 4x+6 steps, never reading R; k full rounds take (x, 0, y+2k) to (x+4k, 0, y).

claims.title: Phase starts and the list of blocks
claims.text: At the records in D of the first 2·109 steps the tape is 0^inf D> 0 a^x j a^y s a^m1 s a^m2 .... New phases start with x = 2 and y = 3, 11, 17, 100, 35, 17, 107, 4, 118, 422, 177, 808, 339, 1312, 2049, 394, 106, ...; the lists behind them are made of pairs of block lengths that grow about threefold from one sweep to the next (3, 11; 9, 41; 35, 123; 105, 377; 51, 107; 153, 329; 977, 3393; 2939, 10179).

claims.title: Rounds with the junction further in, and at the right end
claims.text: mid_round_0: 0^inf D> 0 a^(a+2) s a^b 0 a^(c+1) R → 0^inf D> 0 a^(a+1) s a^(b+3) 1 a^c R in 4a+4b+38 steps (mid_round_1: junction 1 → 0, 4a+4b+34 steps), and the same with one or two blocks s a^(d+2) between, each adding 4d+28 steps (mid_round_j_1, mid_round_j_2). tail_round: 0^inf D> 0 a^(a+2) s a^(f+2) (1001100)^n 1 0^inf → the same with a^(a+1) and (1001100)^(n+1), in 4a+4f+24n+46 steps, and with one or two blocks between. For all lengths and every R.

claims.title: An accelerated simulator, checked against the machine
claims.text: c/m5fast.c applies the three kinds of rounds in one stroke wherever the tape has their form (with any number of blocks between; the step counts follow the same pattern), and simulates the rest. Run beside the plain machine it agrees in tape and state at all 13,356 records in D on the left (every jump included) up to 1.015·1011 steps.

claims.title: No halt to 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: From blank tape c/m5fast reaches 1012 steps without a halt (26 minutes; the visited tape is then about 2·106 cells wide). The rounds it jumps over are the long ones; the steps it still simulates are those where the junction crosses a separator or meets the tail, a bounded number of rounds each, every one costing a sweep of the tape.

claims.title: Why the blocks triple
claims.text: While the junction sits in a block after a separator, every round moves one word from the block after the junction to the block before it and adds two more there (b → b+3, c → c−1). So a block of c words that the junction passes leaves 3c words plus what was there before, which matches the pairs seen earlier (3, 11 → 9, 41 → 35, 123, ...); the first block pays for it, one word a round. What happens when the junction reaches a separator, or the first block runs out, is still simulated, not decoded.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.52×10<sup>13</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.52×1013 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 683 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The only halting transition is C reading 1; none of the proved rounds can halt, so a halt could only come in the short stretches where the junction crosses a separator, meets the tail, or the first block runs out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a list of numbers on its tape, written as blocks of the pair 10, and every sweep of the head over the list multiplies them by about three.

facts.text: No halt, followed exactly by jumping over proved rounds (checked against the machine to 10<sup>11</sup>).
Junction in the first block, further in, or none: proved in Lean for every size.
A block the junction passes comes back three times as long.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.573). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 72,856 cells (62,352 left of the start, 1,095 right), with a density of 1s of 0.498.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A list of blocks
html:
Write a = 10 and s = 01100. Left of the start the tape reads

0^inf D> 0 a^x j a^y s a^m1 s a^m2 s ...

At the left end the head moves the block a^y over, two a's added on the left for each one taken on the right, flipping the junction cell j each time (Lean: half_round_0, half_round_1, rounds). This costs about x steps per a, so the visited tape grows like the square root of the time.

sections.heading: Times three
html: When the block runs out the head sweeps into the list. Blocks it passes come back about three times longer: pairs 3, 11 become 9, 41, then 35, 123, then 105, 377; the pair 51, 107 becomes 153, 329. The exact rule, and how the next first block is made, is the open part. The only halting transition is C reading 1.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: list of blocks tripled by sweeps
summary: A list of blocks of 10 separated by 01100 with a junction moving through it; each passing of the junction triples a block. Three kinds of rounds proved in Lean, accelerated run without a halt. Open.
